newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Barrick sees Busang deal by next week.
newsitem.headline: Barrick sees Busang deal by next week.

text.p: Gold giant Barrick Gold Corp is expected to strike a deal with Bre-X Minerals Ltd over the Busang gold find in Indonesia's East Kalimantan early next week, the Kompas newspaper reported on Friday.

Barrick corporate communications director David Wynne-Morgan was quoted by the newsaper as saying development of the mine, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 47 million ounces of gold, could begin by mid-1997.
He said initial investment would total $1.5 billion.
A Barrick official said Wynne-Morgan left Jakarta for Toronto early on Friday.
Wynne-Morgan was quoted by Kompas as saying in an interview that Barrick had the expertise and funds for the project.
"We made presentations to the Ministry of Mines and Energy six months ago. They (the ministry) saw that we had the funds, expertise and technology," he was quoted as saying.

He said that if the Indonesian government was to choose a new candidate (to partner Bre-X) through international tenders, the process would take a long time, causing the project to be delayed further.

Canada's Bre-X, which owns the dominant share in the Busang field, said on Tuesday that it has been advised by the Indonesian government to reach a settlement with Barrick, also of Canada, by December 4.
Indonesia wants Barrick to take a majority 75 percent stake in Busang with Bre-X holding 25 percent, Calgary-based Bre-X said last Tuesday.
Bre-X also said the Ministry of Mines and Energy "would appreciate if the parties could consider a 10 percent participation being given to the Indonesian government".

Barrick has teamed up with a construction company in the Citra Group of President Suharto's eldest daughter, Siti Hardianti Rukmana, in what Barrick had said was a partnership "to prepare us for a potential mining development project".
Bre-X has entered into a partnership agreement with PT Panutan Duta of the Panutan Group run by Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto.
Under this agreement, PT Panutan would receive $40 million over 40 months plus a 10 percent stake in the richest parts of Busang.
On Barrick's tie-up with the Citra Group, Wynne-Morgan was quoted as saying details had not been worked out yet but he added that the local company had the necessary construction expertise.
On the alliance between Bre-X and PT Panutan, he said he could not understand the arrangement as PT Panutan would be getting a stake in Busang plus cash for "not doing anything".
"It would be different if they (Panutan) are investing (in the project)," he added.
Wynne-Morgan also said it was unfair for the government to seek a 10-percent stake in Busang. "It's like a tax, and I have never heard of such a thing before."

Local businessman Jusuf Merukh, who claims 40 percent of Busang, said on Wednesday he had delayed a $1.9 billion lawsuit against Bre-X, to settle their ownership dispute, until December 4. "Bre-X has asked me to extend my (lawsuit) deadline to December 4 (from November 22)," he said.
"It's because they are busy...possibly because of the talks with Barrick."
